operations.notes: Workspace-visible built-in and custom statuses are authenticated and returned with Jira status-category beans; expanded legacy fields and permission nuances remain.
Status lookup supports workspace-visible IDs and case-insensitive names with exact not-found behavior; project-specific visibility remains.
The three Jira status categories require authentication and return stable IDs, keys, names, and colors.
Category lookup accepts Jira IDs and keys with exact not-found behavior.

Administrators can atomically delete 1 to 50 unused workspace statuses; built-ins and statuses referenced by work, boards, workflow drafts/published definitions, or automation reject and roll back the complete batch. Exact project-admin permissions remain.
Repeated status IDs return workspace-visible JiraStatus resources with GLOBAL or PROJECT scope. Exact missing-ID/error and permission parity remains.

Administrators can atomically create validated GLOBAL or PROJECT status batches with descriptions, categories, scope-local duplicate detection, project ownership checks, rollback, and audit evidence. Exact project-admin permissions remain.

Administrators can atomically update custom status batches, including simultaneous name swaps, while preserving GLOBAL or PROJECT ownership with built-in protection, rollback, and audit evidence. Exact project-admin permissions remain.

Repeated names return case-insensitive scope-visible matches, with projectId selecting that project's statuses and an omitted selector returning global statuses. Exact Jira permission filtering remains.
Search supports text, category, projectId, includeGlobalStatuses, startAt/maxResults paging, totals, isLast, and filter-preserving nextPage links. Exact Jira permission filtering remains.
Returns paged issue type IDs observed using the status in the requested workspace project with strict status/project validation; scheme-derived unused issue types remain.
Returns opaque-token pages of workspace projects whose issues, boards, or active workflow use the status; workflow-scheme-only associations remain.
Returns opaque-token pages of active project workflows using the status; unassigned and workflow-scheme draft usages remain.
Returns durable ENQUEUED, RUNNING, COMPLETE, FAILED, and CANCELLED task progress and results to the submitter or a workspace administrator with Jira epoch-millisecond fields.
Cancels submitter- or administrator-visible enqueued and running tasks with HTTP 202; cancellation before the worker commit atomically rolls back domain changes, while finished tasks return HTTP 400.
Deletes workspace-owned inactive workflows atomically with audit evidence and rejects system, project-active, published-scheme, and draft-scheme references; project-scoped workflows remain.
Returns opaque-cursor pages of issue type IDs that resolve to the workflow in a workspace-scoped project, including default mapping fallback.
Returns opaque-cursor pages of workspace project IDs whose published scheme resolves the workflow; additional project fields and Jira cursor encoding remain.
Returns opaque-cursor pages of workspace published scheme IDs that reference the workflow through default or issue-type mappings; draft usage remains.

Resolves workflows by workflow ID or project and issue type, validates selectors, and reports the resolved GLOBAL or PROJECT editor scope, project types, and executable actor restriction, API-only restriction, typed field-value, previous-status, separation-of-duties, parent/child blocking, required/changed/single-value/regular-expression/date-comparison/date-window/history/permission and Advanced Forms attached/submitted validators, change-assignee, system/custom field-update, same-or-parent field-copy, durable registered-webhook trigger, and transition-screen rules; remaining system/ecosystem rules remain.

Atomically creates up to 20 validated GLOBAL or PROJECT directed workflows and related statuses with generated IDs, layouts/properties, versions, scoped Jira resources, executable conditions, validators, post-functions and transition screens, rollback, and audit; remaining rules remain.

Returns structured ERROR validation for GLOBAL/PROJECT ownership, names and statuses, sizes, references, designer layouts, directed topology, nested conditions, validators, post-functions, transition screens, conflicts, and level filtering; remaining rules and non-directed transitions remain.
Returns the authenticated user default editor contract as NEW because ZZIRA exposes its new workflow editor; per-user legacy editor preference remains.

Previews project-associated global or project workflows by ID, name, and issue type, returning scoped resources, query contexts, layouts, topology, versions, statuses, and executable conditions, validators, post-functions and transition screens; remaining rules and approval configuration remain.

Searches published global and project-scoped workflows with scope/project/activity filters, validated paging and name ordering, related statuses, versions, designer layouts, transition expansion, and executable condition, validator, post-function, and screen configuration; created/updated ordering remains.

Atomically creates related scoped statuses, migrates active work with sync actions, and updates layouts plus executable conditions, validators, post-functions and transition screens with optimistic versions, rollback, and audit; remaining rules, mixed-scope batches, and queued tasks remain.

Returns structured validation for existence and preserved scope, optimistic versions, scoped statuses, layouts, topology, mappings, executable conditions, validators, post-functions and transition screens without mutation; remaining rules and mixed-scope batches remain.
Lists workspace workflow schemes with Jira page and workflow-name mapping shapes; startAt/maxResults filtering remains.
Creates audited workspace schemes with validated default and issue-type workflow mappings; additional classic Jira flags remain.
Returns workflow-scheme associations for repeated workspace project IDs; Jira default-scheme null semantics remain.
Assigns a scheme transactionally when every existing issue status is already supported; clients use the switch operation when explicit replacement mappings are required.
Validates and enqueues a durable Jira 303 task that atomically switches a project to a published scheme and migrates incompatible issues with synchronized status actions.
Reads deduplicated workspace schemes by scheme and project IDs with workflow metadata, scope, grouped issue types, and document versions; task-in-progress metadata remains.

Optimistically validates and enqueues a published-scheme update, then atomically applies workflow and issue-type status replacements, sync actions, audit, version increment, and task completion in a restart-safe worker.
Calculates required status mappings by issue type and source/target workflow from affected workspace project issues with deterministic status metadata; unused workflow-status differences remain.
Deletes inactive workspace schemes with audit evidence and rejects active schemes; default-scheme protection remains.
Returns published or requested draft scheme configuration with workspace isolation and not-found behavior; expanded draft metadata remains.
Validates and saves default and issue-type mappings as an inactive runtime draft; updateDraftIfNeeded and direct inactive updates remain.
Copies the published workspace scheme into an isolated audited draft and rejects duplicate draft creation; expanded modification metadata remains.
Resets a published workspace scheme to the built-in default workflow with impact validation, versioning, and audit; schemes without a platform default remain unsupported.
Returns the published default workflow by Jira workflow name with workspace isolation.
Validates and updates the published default workflow with assigned-project impact checks, versioning, and audit; updateDraftIfNeeded remains.
Discards an existing workspace draft with audit evidence and leaves the published runtime unchanged; Jira default-scheme semantics remain.
Returns only an existing isolated draft with workflow-name mappings and strict workspace scoping; expanded modification metadata remains.
Partially updates and validates draft name, description, default workflow, and issue-type mappings without changing runtime; updateDraftIfNeeded remains.
Resets the draft default to the built-in workflow and returns the updated draft; schemes without a platform default remain unsupported.
Returns the draft default workflow by Jira workflow name with draft and workspace validation.
Validates and updates the draft default by workflow name with audit evidence; updateDraftIfNeeded remains.
Deletes one draft issue-type override and returns the updated draft with strict missing-mapping behavior.
Returns one draft issue-type to workflow-name mapping with strict missing-draft and missing-mapping behavior.
Validates and saves one draft issue-type workflow override with workspace isolation and audit evidence.
Validates and enqueues draft publication, then atomically applies per-issue-type status replacements, sync actions, audit, version increment, and task completion in a restart-safe worker.
Removes every draft issue-type mapping for a named workflow and safely resets that workflow as default; Jira default-scheme nuances remain.
Returns issue types and default membership for a named workflow in an isolated draft; omitted workflowName behavior remains.
Moves a named workflow mapping across validated issue types and optionally makes it the draft default; updateDraftIfNeeded remains.
Deletes a published issue-type override with assigned-project impact validation, versioning, and audit.
Returns one published issue-type to workflow-name mapping with strict missing-mapping behavior.
Validates and saves one published issue-type override with assigned-project impact checks, versioning, and audit.
Removes published issue-type mappings for a named workflow, resets it as default when needed, and validates assigned project impact.
Returns issue types and default membership for a named published workflow; omitted workflowName behavior remains.
Moves a published named-workflow mapping across validated issue types with impact checks, versioning, and audit; updateDraftIfNeeded remains.
Returns opaque-cursor pages of workspace project IDs assigned to the scheme with maxResults validation; additional project fields remain.

Stores valid build snapshots with monotonic update ordering, issue-key/ID associations, per-build rejection, unknown associations, provider properties, issue/release UI evidence and the documented 202 result; Connect JWT scopes, rate limits and every optional field constraint remain.
Deletes property-matched builds with optional update-sequence protection and the documented accepted response; execution is immediate rather than asynchronous.
Accepts idempotent keyed deletion with optional inclusive update-sequence protection; execution is immediate rather than asynchronous.
Returns the current sequence-ordered build payload by its composite key, including direct and cloudId proxy routing; Connect JWT scopes and rate limits remain.

Stores valid deployment snapshots with monotonic update ordering, issue-key/ID associations, per-deployment rejection, provider properties, environment metadata, issue/release UI evidence and the documented 202 result; Connect JWT scopes, rate limits and every optional field constraint remain.
Deletes property-matched deployments with optional update-sequence protection and the documented accepted response; execution is immediate rather than asynchronous.
Accepts idempotent keyed deletion with optional inclusive update-sequence protection; execution is immediate rather than asynchronous.
Returns the current sequence-ordered deployment payload by its composite key, including direct and cloudId proxy routing; Connect JWT scopes and rate limits remain.
Returns the documented deployment key, timestamp, allowed status and detail array for stored deployments; configurable deployment gates and blocked issue details remain.

Stores repositories, commits, branches and pull requests with monotonic update ordering, issue-key/ID associations, unknown-key reporting, preventTransitions, browser evidence and branch-created workflow execution; Connect JWT scopes, rate limits and every field constraint remain.
Deletes repositories matching all validated provider properties with Jira-compatible accepted response; asynchronous execution and Connect JWT scopes remain.
Checks property containment with optional update-sequence filtering and validated query cardinality; Connect JWT scopes and rate limits remain.
Accepts idempotent repository deletion and honors optional monotonic deletion sequence; execution is immediate rather than asynchronous.
Returns the currently persisted repository with its most recent current entities after ordered updates and deletes; exact response truncation ties remain.
Accepts idempotent commit, branch and pull_request deletion with optional monotonic sequence protection; execution is immediate rather than asynchronous.
Create and round-trip behavior is tested; broader identity and cursor semantics remain.
Manual-rule search is not implemented.
Manual-rule search is not implemented.
Manual-rule invocation is not implemented.
Listing is tested; cursor expiry and central-host authentication remain.
Supported summary filters and pagination are tested.
Disabled-rule deletion and error behavior are tested.
Rule and connection round trips plus sensitive-field redaction are tested.
Replacement with path-UUID preservation is tested.
Scope replacement is tested for the Jira site gateway.
Enable and disable behavior is tested.
Template-based rule creation is not implemented.
Template search is not implemented.
Template search is not implemented.
Template retrieval is not implemented.
Bearer-authenticated discovery is implemented for the site served by this ZZIRA instance.
The organization bean and related links are implemented for authorized site administrators.

Visible browser use is recorded after two seconds and returned per product with exact IDs, mapped keys, UTC dates and timestamps, organization-add time, and opaque cursors; long-term aggregation and central-host rate limiting remain.
Organization DNS claims return exact domain resource and claim shapes with opaque paging; cross-organization ownership and provider-managed claims remain.
Domain detail reports normalized name, DNS claim type, lifecycle status, self link, and exact not-found behavior.
The action catalog covers every organization mutation currently emitted by ZZIRA; locale negotiation and future product action groups remain.

Immutable organization audit events support text, action, actor, IP, product, location, time, limit, and cursor filters with Jira-shaped resources; request metadata capture and central rate limiting remain.
Polling returns ascending or descending audit pages with processedAt, time bounds, limits, and reusable opaque cursors; long-lived keyset cursor state remains.
Event detail returns actor, target context, organization container, immutable attributes, links, and exact not-found behavior.
Policy listing returns rule and resource state with type filtering, metadata, self/next links, and opaque paging; runtime enforcement remains.
Policy creation validates nested wire shape, type, status, IP/CIDR or residency rule values, product ownership, duplicates, and commits audit evidence atomically.
Policy deletion cascades resource associations, preserves audit evidence, and returns the documented accepted/not-found behavior.
Policy detail returns type, name, status, rule, resource application state, metadata, links, and not-found behavior.
Whole-policy update validates matching IDs, rule values and resources, replaces state atomically, and records audit evidence.
Resource attachment accepts product ARIs owned by the organization with metadata and ticket links and returns updated applied state.
Resource removal is audited and returns the documented no-content/not-found behavior.
Resource update replaces metadata and links for the exact policy/resource pair and returns the updated policy.
Validation confirms a stored policy passed rule and organization-resource constraints; asynchronous application checks remain.
Managed-account listing reports global account state, directory-derived billable access, identity, and opaque paging validation.
Organization-admin assignment is validated, persisted immediately, and audited.
Organization-admin revocation is persisted immediately and audited.
Direct site and product role assignment accepts Atlassian role IDs and discovered resource ARIs.
Direct site and product role revocation is implemented and audited.
Internal directory listing and opaque pagination are implemented; directory filters remain.
Group listing, searchTerm, counts, management access and opaque pagination are implemented.
Internal group creation and duplicate-name conflicts are implemented and audited.
Group count implements directory, member, group, resource-owner, resource-ID, role-ID, and name filters.
Group search implements documented filters, mutual exclusions, sorting, expansions, multi-directory scope, and opaque pagination.
Group statistics report internal group-type and management totals for one or all authorized directories.
Group deletion atomically removes memberships and role grants and records an audit event.
Group details include management access and live user/resource counts.
Directory-scoped membership addition, conflicts and auditing are implemented.
Directory-scoped membership removal, not-found behavior and auditing are implemented.
Group role assignments support cursor paging and directory, resource owner, resource ID, and role filters.
Group product access accepts Atlassian resource ARIs, updates effective access immediately, and is audited.
Group product access revocation updates effective access immediately and is audited.
Directory user listing supports searchTerm and opaque cursor pagination.
Directory user counts support the implemented searchTerm filter.
Directory-user search implements stored profile, identity, group, lifecycle, MFA, domain, resource, role, expansion, sort, and pagination fields.
User statistics report account lifecycle and effective role counts for one or all authorized directories.
Directory removal revokes membership, group links, and scoped direct roles atomically; sessions and API tokens are revoked after the final active directory is removed.
Restoration reactivates the selected directory membership without changing global account state and is audited.
Effective user assignments combine direct and group-derived roles and report assignment methods.
Suspension immediately denies access through the selected directory while preserving other organizations; sessions and API tokens are revoked after the final active directory is suspended.
Directory account details report stored identity, profile, account state, and directory membership state.
Invitations atomically provision provider-ready accounts, product roles, groups, audit evidence, and optional durable SMTP delivery; paid-license limits remain.
Product workspace discovery returns Jira Software, Jira Service Management, and Confluence ARIs with strict cursor paging.
